verdict.summary: Sign in with Yahoo (openid, email, profile) is self-serve, but the mail scopes (mail-r, mail-w) used for IMAP/SMTP are 'not available for self-served setup': you apply through Yahoo's developer access form, show you meet its security and privacy requirements, and sign a commercial access agreement. Yahoo publishes no review timeline, and there is no REST Mail API, only IMAP/SMTP with OAUTHBEARER.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: An OIDC sign-in app works in under an hour, but mail scopes don't work even for your own account until Yahoo approves the app. You can build the IMAP logic against your own mailbox with an app password in the meantime. The range is a guess, since Yahoo states no timeline.

timeToProd.assumes: An agent that reads (mail-r) or sends/modifies (mail-w) a user's Yahoo mail over IMAP/SMTP. Sign-in-only apps are live the same day.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Yahoo's manual review of the developer access request, then the signed Commercial Access Agreement

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Neither Yahoo nor Nylas gives a timeline. The range is our estimate for a manual, contract-based approval and should be read as unverified.

verdict.cost: No fee is published. Access requires agreeing to Yahoo's additional commercial terms (the Commercial Access Agreement).

prerequisites.item: A Yahoo account to own the app in the developer console (YDN)
prerequisites.why: Apps are created at developer.yahoo.com/apps, and the access form asks for your YDN account.

prerequisites.item: A business identity, privacy policy and evidence of minimum security standards
prerequisites.why: Yahoo says applicants must provide clear information about the identity of the app and requester, and demonstrate they meet minimum security standards to be accepted.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Yahoo doesn't name a specific assessment (such as CASA) or say how security is verified.

prerequisites.item: A use case that serves Yahoo users directly, with no resale, ad targeting or profiling
prerequisites.why: Data may not be transferred or sold, used for advertising segments, or used for profiling, monetization or email engagement tracking.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The policy doesn't mention AI or LLM processing specifically.

prerequisites.item: An IMAP/SMTP client that supports SASL OAUTHBEARER (and XOAUTH2 for SMTP)
prerequisites.why: Yahoo offers no proprietary Mail REST API. Mail access is IMAP (imap.mail.yahoo.com:993) and SMTP (smtp.mail.yahoo.com:465) with OAuth bearer tokens.

scopeTiers.impact: Identity only. The discovery document lists only openid, openid2, profile and email as supported scopes.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: scopes_supported in the live discovery document on 2026-10-20.

scopeTiers.impact: Read mail over IMAP. Requires the developer access request and agreement. Until approval, community reports say sign-in succeeds but mail access is refused.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 'sign-in works, mail refused' behaviour comes from a community project and is unverified.

scopeTiers.impact: Needed to send via SMTP or move/flag/delete messages. Same approval path as mail-r. Pick Read/Write in the app's Mail permission.
Same commercial access program as mail. Request them on the same form if your agent needs them.

steps.title: Sign in to the Yahoo developer console
steps.detail: Use the Yahoo account that will own the integration. Its email is what you'll put on the access form.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: https://developer.yahoo.com/apps/create/ returned 302 to login.yahoo.com on 2026-10-20. We did not sign in.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Enter name, description, homepage and redirect URI(s). Choose Confidential client, tick OpenID Connect Email and Profile, and pick Mail Read or Read/Write if the option is shown. Save the client ID and secret. Scopes are fixed on the app, not sent in the authorize request.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Field names come from the Nylas guide. Yahoo's own docs don't show the form.

steps.title: Draft the access request
steps.detail: Write up the company identity, the exact use case (how the agent uses mail on the user's behalf), the scopes needed, data storage and retention, security controls, and a statement that data isn't sold, used for ad targeting or profiling.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Yahoo doesn't publish the form's fields. The content is drawn from the policy's requirements.

steps.title: Submit the Yahoo Mail API access form
steps.detail: Fill in the form with your YDN account email, set API required to IMAP (and CalDAV/CardDAV if needed), and paste the drafted justification. Questions go to mail-api@yahooinc.com.

steps.title: Build IMAP logic with an app password while you wait
steps.detail: Have the developer generate an app password on their own account and use it to build the IMAP fetch/search and SMTP send code. Swap in OAUTHBEARER once approved. Don't ship app-password collection to end users.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Nylas documents app passwords as an IMAP option. Using them as a dev stopgap is our suggestion.

steps.title: Yahoo reviews the request
steps.detail: Yahoo emails when it approves the request or needs more details. No timeline is published.

steps.title: Sign and return the Commercial Access Agreement
steps.detail: Yahoo sends a 'Yahoo Mail Products Commercial Access Agreement'. Have someone with signing authority review and return it.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://api.login.yahoo.com/oauth2/request_auth?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code&state=.... Exchange at POST https://api.login.yahoo.com/oauth2/get_token with HTTP Basic client auth. PKCE S256 is advertised in the discovery document.

steps.title: Connect to IMAP/SMTP with OAUTHBEARER
steps.detail: Check the CAPABILITY response for AUTH=OAUTHBEARER, then AUTHENTICATE OAUTHBEARER on imap.mail.yahoo.com:993. Send the IMAP ID NAME as the partner name or ID assigned during approval. For SMTP use smtp.mail.yahoo.com:465 with whichever of OAUTHBEARER/XOAUTH2 the server advertises.

steps.title: Test with a non-developer Yahoo account
steps.detail: Connect a second account, confirm the consent screen lists mail access, and confirm IMAP login succeeds. Then revoke the app from Yahoo account settings and check your app handles the dead refresh token.

agentCanDo: Draft the access request and data-use statement
Implement the code flow and refresh logic
Write IMAP/SMTP code with SASL OAUTHBEARER
Check the discovery document and IMAP capabilities
humanMustDo: Create the app in the Yahoo developer console
Follow up with mail-api@yahooinc.com if review stalls

blockers.symptom: Mail scopes don't show up, or can't be enabled, in the developer console
blockers.cause: IMAP, CalDAV and CardDAV scopes are not available for self-served setup.
blockers.fix: Submit the developer access form. Approved scopes then appear in your app profile.

blockers.symptom: Sign-in succeeds but IMAP AUTHENTICATE fails / mail access is refused
blockers.cause: The app hasn't been approved for mail-r/mail-w yet.
blockers.fix: Wait for approval, then have users re-consent so their tokens carry the mail scope.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: From a community project's PR, not Yahoo docs.

blockers.symptom: 'Bad scope' / invalid scope error at the authorize step
blockers.cause: The requested scope isn't in the app's registered permissions, or both mail-r and mail-w were requested together.
blockers.fix: Request only the permissions configured on the app, and use mail-w alone for read/write.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The mail-r + mail-w conflict is stated by Nylas for its connector. The 'Bad scope' string is from forum reports.

blockers.symptom: Login is inconsistent right after adding a redirect URI
blockers.cause: Redirect URI registration can take up to 24 hours to propagate.
blockers.fix: Register production redirect URIs a day ahead of launch.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Stated by Nylas, not in Yahoo's docs.

blockers.cause: The user revoked access, or you kept an old refresh token after Yahoo issued a new one (the old one is revoked).
blockers.fix: Store the refresh token returned on every refresh, and re-prompt the user if it's revoked.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The invalid_grant string is the standard OAuth error, not quoted by Yahoo.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 1 hour. Refresh tokens are long-lived, survive password changes, and may be rotated on refresh, so persist the newest one.
Scopes are configured on the app, not passed in the authorize request, so changing mail permissions changes what every new consent grants.
Yahoo and AOL are separate namespaces and need separate client credentials, even though they share a parent company.
There is no Yahoo Mail REST/JSON API. Search, threading and parsing are your IMAP client's job, which adds real engineering for an agent.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Yahoo says it no longer supports proprietary Mail APIs.

nuances.text: Data-use terms bar resale, ad targeting, and profiling for personalization, monetization or engagement tracking. AI processing isn't addressed, so describe any LLM use plainly in your request.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The advice to disclose LLM use is our inference.
